articles.title: Insólito momento en el fútbol colombiano: travesaño se desplomó y golpeó al arquero en mitad de un penalti
articles.standfirst: Así fue el insólito accidente en el Torneo BetPlay donde un travesaño cayó sobre el arquero
articles.summary: Así fue el insólito accidente en el Torneo BetPlay donde un travesaño cayó sobre el arquero
articles.body: El fútbol profesional colombiano suele regalar momentos llenos de emoción, talento y, en ocasiones, situaciones tan insólitas que rozan lo surrealista. En esta oportunidad, un partido válido por el Torneo BetPlay (segunda división) se convirtió en el centro de atención global debido a un cómico y a la vez peligroso incidente que tuvo como protagonista al arquero visitante y al propio arco del estadio. Los hechos ocurrieron durante el duelo entre el Leones FC y el Atlético FC. El compromiso transcurría en medio de la intensidad propia de la competencia, cuando el juez central señaló una pena máxima que obligaba a una tensión absoluta en el terreno de juego. Mientras el guardameta del conjunto visitante, Miguel Arboleda, se preparaba para afrontar el cobro desde los doce pasos e intentaba desconcentrar al cobrador saltando y tocando los postes de su portería, ocurrió lo inesperado: el travesaño de la estructura cedió de manera repentina y terminó desprendiéndose por completo, cayendo directamente sobre la humanidad del arquero. El inusual suceso obligó a detener las acciones de inmediato. El guardameta, visiblemente sorprendido e incómodo por el momento, quedó atrapado por instantes bajo el madero ante la mirada atónita de sus compañeros, rivales y el cuerpo arbitral, en una escena que de inmediato se filtró en las redes sociales y escaló a portales internacionales por lo precaria de la situación. Más allá del insólito momento que le dio la vuelta a las redes y generó burlas y críticas sobre las condiciones de los escenarios deportivos en el país, el encuentro continuó tras solucionar el inconveniente técnico. Irónicamente, la jugada posterior al incidente coronó la noche atípica: aunque el cobrador de Leones tuvo la oportunidad de descontar en el marcador sobre el tramo final del compromiso (minuto 87), el remate se desaprovechó, sentenciando una victoria contundente del Atlético FC por 0-3 con una destacada actuación y triplete del delantero Alejandro Oñate. Sin embargo, el resultado deportivo terminó quedando en un segundo plano absoluto. La imagen del arquero derribando —sin proponérselo— su propio arco se consolidó como uno de los "bochornos" y momentos más virales del año en el fútbol colombiano, reabriendo el debate sobre el mantenimiento y la calidad de la infraestructura en los estadios del rentado nacional.

images.caption: Arquero del fútbol colombiano bota su propio arco en un penal y causa bochorno internacional. Twitter

articles.title: Fulham 2-3 Crystal Palace: Alvaro Arbeloa booed off after third defeat in row
articles.summary: Fulham arebooed off by some supporters following the 3-2 Premier League defeat by Crystal Palace at Craven Cottage.
articles.body:
Fulham were booed off by some supporters following the 3-2 Premier League defeat by Crystal Palace at Craven Cottage.

Having led twice in the first half, Alvaro Arbeloa's side fell to a third consecutive Premier League defeat since he replaced Marco Silva, who joined Benfica in the summer following five years in charge.

Josh King and summer signing Cesar Palacios scored in the first half, but a goal in each half from Tyrick Mitchell levelled the match twice before substitute Ben Chilwell scored the winner three minutes into his second Palace stint.

It leaves Fulham as one of only two sides to have lost their opening three Premier League games this season, alongside Coventry City .

It follows defeat at Sunderland and at home to Chelsea , which also finished 3-2.

Liverpool and Manchester United are next on Fulham 's league fixture list before the extended September and October international break.

"We didn't deserve to lose this game," Arbeloa told BBC's Match of the Day.

"My players did everything - good attitude, they were brave, so many chances to score more goals.

"They [Palace] took their chances - in the end football is about that.

"We did many good things to win the game. It was similar against Chelsea but we lose.

"For the players it's a difficult situation, difficult moment, but I am very proud of them."

Chilwell scores on Palace return in win at Fulham

Fulham enjoyed a better expected goals (xG) of 3.13 than Palace (1.97), and also ran Chelsea close on the opening weekend.

But that does not stop the table reading three matches played, three defeats, zero points.

It led to booing from some Fulham fans, as well as chants questioning the team's performance.

Arbeloa will be no stranger to pressure. His playing career included more than 350 appearances for Real Madrid, Deportivo la Coruna, Liverpool and West Ham.

He also won 56 caps for Spain and was part of their side that won two European Championships and a World Cup between 2008 and 2012.

Arbeloa got the job following four months as Real's caretaker manager, taking charge of the final 28 matches of last season following Xabi Alonso's departure.

In that time he oversaw 18 wins, two draws and eight defeats.

As a former defender, the Spaniard will have wanted to avoid conceding three goals, especially in the manner they did.

"We were really unlucky in this goal [second Palace goal," Arbeloa said.

If Fulham can keep creating chances in the way they did against Palace, the victories should come. But the prospect of being on zero - or very few - points at the international break is a real one.

Arbeloa faces meetings with two of his former clubs next. A trip to Liverpool comes before a home Carabao Cup third-round tie with the Hammers and a league meeting with Manchester United .

Only six Premier League teams have started a season with five straight defeats. Of them, only two went on to avoid relegation.

Fulham made seven signings this summer. Of them, three followed Arbeloa in swapping the Bernabeu for Craven Cottage in Palacios, Gonzalo Garcia and deadline-day arrival Manuel Angel.

Palacios and Garcia have started all three league matches, while Northern Ireland midfielder Shea Charles was also handed a first league start against Palace following his £30m move from Southampton.

Palacios took his goal well, converting on the follow-up after Palace goalkeeper Dean Henderson could only spill Jaydee Canvot's attempted clearance into his path.

Garcia, trusted to be Fulham 's main source of goals this season, was unable to add to his tally against Palace, but did score on his debut against Chelsea and as a substitute in their EFL Cup second-round win over AFC Wimbledon three days later.

"Cesar Palacios and Gonzalo Garcia both had a great game. Cesar scored a goal, and for Gonzalo another great performance," Arbeloa added.

"Good effort from Gonzalo. That's the spirit I want from my players - the striker making a sprint to try and save a goal.

"With that spirit and character, if we play in this way the victories will come."

images.caption: Image caption, Cesar Palacios scored his first Fulham goal shortly before half-time

articles.title: North Texas' Stunning Roster, Coaching Staff Turnover Spotlighted During CFB Opener vs. Indiana
articles.summary: The North Texas Mean Green football team is a veritable Ship of Theseus.
articles.body:
The North Texas Mean Green football team is a veritable Ship of Theseus.

The 2026 roster didn't return a single starter from last season's team, per the Fox broadcast of Saturday's matchup against Indiana, has 72 entirely new players on its roster and lost 18 coaches and 19 players to Oklahoma State alone, as Eric Morris led quite the exodus when he took over as the Cowboys' new head coach.

Watch: CFB QB's face bloodied after facemask penalty

The Mean Green then completely rebuilt the roster under new head coach Neal Brown, and that new-look unit was tasked with facing the defending national champions to start the 2026 season.

Roster turnover has become the norm in college football during the transfer portal era, but North Texas was certainly at the extreme end of the trend this offseason.

articles.title: Colorado School of Mines and Washburn end their game in a 16-16 tie to avoid an hours-long heat delay
articles.summary: The game was originally scheduled for a noon kickoff before it was rescheduled a second time for 9 a.m.
articles.body:
Blame the heat for a tie between Colorado School of Mines and Washburn on Saturday.

The two Division II teams agreed to end their Saturday morning game tied at 16-16 after Colorado School of Mines missed a potential game-winning field goal late in the fourth quarter. The game was set to go to overtime, but the wet bulb temperature had already exceeded the Mid-America Intercollegiate Athletics Association's temperature protocols. Washburn, the home team, is a member of the MIAA.

The game had little chance of resuming anytime soon if the teams wanted to play overtime. Thanks to the heat dome that's currently occupying the middle part of the country, the temperature in Topeka, Kansas, was set to be around 100 degrees on Saturday with the heat index not dropping below 95 degrees until after sunset at 7:49 p.m.

The game was originally scheduled for a noon kickoff before it was pushed to 7 p.m. earlier in the week. With a forecast for temperatures still well into the 90s at that time and Colorado School of Mines' travel to take into account, the teams then agreed to play the game at 9 a.m. in an attempt to avoid what ended up happening anyway.

Washburn is now 1-0-1 after a season-opening win against Truman State. Colorado School of Mines is 0-1-1 after the Orediggers lost to Western Oregon to begin the 2026 season.

articles.title: Russell Martin: What next for Leicester City boss after 'sackable performance'?
articles.summary: Tipped for a turnaround in fortunes, the Foxes and their boss continue to falter in the third tier.
articles.body:
"I don't think the manager should get sacked tonight, but that is a sackable performance."

Russell Martin's Leicester City slumped to new depths on Saturday when they were hammered 4-0 at home by Oxford United , conceding three second-half goals in just 20 minutes.

It was their heaviest-ever defeat in the third tier and marked an all-time low in the club's otherwise proud 142-year history, despondent fans told BBC Radio Leicester at full-time.

Not long ago the Foxes were the darlings of English football, a living fairytale after their 2015-16 Premier League title win against all odds.

Many had expected them to stroll through League One after their unexpected relegation last term - their second in as many seasons - but life back in the third tier under the divisive Martin has been far more difficult than envisaged.

Granted, it is still early days, but those who watch the club regularly are already concerned.

"This manager doesn't seem to want to move away, at all, from the pass them to death, that's how we will win a football match," says former Leicester player and BBC Radio Leicester match summariser Matt Piper.

"I'm an advocate of that style when your team is playing well and can execute it in the way that you want it. I'm also an advocate of winning football matches and you can do that in many different ways.

"We have only seen one way from this manager. My fingers are pointing at him this afternoon, even though the team didn't play well.

Martin is already under pressure from sections of the club's fanbase, who made their feelings clear during Saturday's defeat.

Oxford Utd thump Leicester to heap pressure on Martin

Martin's reputation on line as he tries to halt Leicester slide

After five league games, he has just one win with two draws and two defeats.

Following a disastrous spell at Rangers, which lasted just 123 days, and his sacking from Southampton, with whom he earned just one win in 16 Premier League games after leading them to promotion, he too is in need of a revival.

While disappointed with the performance against Oxford, which followed an impressive 2-0 midweek win over potential promotion rivals Plymouth Argyle, he remained steadfast in his commitment to the project at the King Power Stadium.

"I'm not concerned about that happening again," he told BBC Radio Leicester.

"I feel I understand what's happened today with so many young guys and a tough moment. We can't quite get through it and after a big, busy period.

"We will be better for it. We have a week now and we have to make sure we put it right next week."

The Foxes started Saturday's game with five players in the starting XI under the age of 23, including two teenagers.

Their five substitutions were aged 18, 19, 20, 21 and 23.

The number of arrivals and departures at the club since their relegation are both well into double figures.

The club, which is also up for sale, is very much in a period of transition.

Martin rued his side's "naivety and inexperience" in their latest defeat, adding: "We had a lot of players who were doing a third game in a week for the first time in their careers, but it's not an excuse.

"But I think that's the learning now - we have to find a team on the pitch, especially in a three-game week that can deliver a consistent level of aggression and a consistent level of energy because the last three games we have built so much energy, so much feel-good factor about it.

"The players and staff, the fans have been brilliant and we had to build on the win on Tuesday night and today we have done the opposite."

There is a genuine uncertainty about whether Martin will be given the time to try to put things right after such a damaging defeat, as Piper explains.

"If you look back over the years, especially at this football club at managers that we have sacked, that looked like a manager that could get sacked tonight."

images.caption: Image caption, Russell Martin was appointed Leicester City boss on 15 June
Image caption, Plenty of Foxes fans voted with their feet after witnessing another defeat

articles.title: José Alberto: "Me voy muy disgustado porque creo que nos han perjudicado"
articles.standfirst: Se quejó del arbitraje de Quintero González
articles.summary: Se quejó del arbitraje de Quintero González
articles.body: José Alberto valoraba el partido al término del mismo y, además, se quejó del arbitraje al entender que les han perjudicado. Valoración: "Después de marcar dos goles a domicilio con lo difícil que es no podemos perder. Tenemos que mejorar defensivamente Creo que merecimos puntuar". Sobre el gol anulado el técnico asturiano: "Mi jugador no toca a Cárdenas en ningún momento, esto es fútbol no es baloncesto. Creo que el VAR tiene que actuar en esta acción tan manifiesta". Sobre el arbitraje: "Me voy muy disgustado porque creo que nos han perjudicado. El árbitro no me ha querido dar ninguna explicación por el gol anulado". Sabe lo que le ha faltado al equipo: "Hay otro equipo que te aprieta, nos ha faltado tener más posesión, nos hemos quedado muy largos. Estamos faltos de rodaje con varios jugadores".

images.caption: Un serio José Alberto, durante la rueda de prensa Real Racing Club

articles.title: Hull 0-0 Aston Villa: Tigers remain unbeaten as Unai Emery's 200th game in charge fails to bring much-needed goal
articles.summary: Report and free match highlights as Hull draw 0-0 with Aston Villa; Unai Emery's side manage first shot on target all season but spurn huge chances to win; the Tigers remain unbeaten with three consecutive clean sheets in dream start to the season
articles.body:
After an improved performance against Arsenal, Unai Emery was hoping for better fortunes in what was his 200th game in charge of the Villans.

A positive start saw Nicolas Jackson head wide in the opening couple of minutes, before youngster George Hemmings managed the club's first shot on target of the season in the first quarter of an hour.

However, the reigning Europa League champions often lacked the imagination to concern the newly promoted Tigers, who looked the most threatening during the first 45 with their collection of long-range efforts.

That was until the start of the second half, which saw Villa spurn two glorious opportunities.

First, some neat interplay between Emi Buendia and Jackson left John McGinn one-on-one with Konstantinos Tzolakis, only for the Scot to blaze his shot too high. Three minutes later, an even better chance fell for Buendia, who couldn't keep his effort down after being left unmarked inside the penalty area.

From that point on, it was the hosts looked most likely and who should've stolen the points.

Mohamed Belloumi saw a stunning curling effort crash off the crossbar just after the hour mark. Then at the death, Ryan Giles picked out Oli McBurnie inside the penalty area, but the hero from the Championship fluffed his lines when a first Premier League goal for the Tigers looked inevitable.

While not three wins from three, the stalemate does mean that Hull remain unbeaten, something unfathomable at the start of the campaign. Meanwhile, Villa's first point is enough for them to climb out of the bottom three.

Emery taking positives from another goalless outing

Despite failing to score for the third successive match, Unai Emery was pleased with what he saw from his Aston Villa side as they continue to regroup after losing several key players.

"I'm positive. The result is not enough but how we planned and how we played and how we created some chances to score, I think we deserved more," Emery told Sky Sports .

"We avoided mistakes we made before. We avoided transitions. Through our positioning and keeping possession we tried to dominate and then in the end we had the chances to win.

"Of course they are very excited in front of their home supporters. They had some chances, but overall in 90 minutes, I can feel comfortable with how we are progressing."

Despite the positivity, the Spaniard admitted there was no avoiding that his side needed to be more clinical in the final third moving forward.

"We weren't clinical. We had four very good chances to score and of course if we do the match can change. When you don't you have to be careful defensively of the transition."

Hull's incredible start continues to blow Jakirovic away

While many tipped them to be the favourites for relegation, Hull's incredible start to the season continued to be the story of the third weekend of the new Premier League campaign. Even boss Sergej Jakirovic couldn't hide the fact that he would've jumped at the chance to take seven points away from his first nine.

"Amazing. If somebody offered this to me at the start of the season I would sign it immediately," Jakirovic said post-match.

"Especially with who we were against. This is a great example for us that we have to continue like this as it shows us that we can compete at this level."

He also has high hopes for his Deadline Day arrivals, who feature in different capacities at the MKM Stadium.

Sorba Thomas and Brooke Norton-Cuffy made their debuts off the bench following their deadline day arrivals, while Robinio Vaz and Christos Mouzakitis remained on the bench. Tim Iroegbunam and Ilyas Ansah were not part of the squad, but were also signed on the final day of the window.

"They are very high potential players," Jakirovic added.

"They need time. Okay, Sorba came from Stoke with pre-season, but some players they didn't have a pre-season. This is right now a problem."

200 up for Emery, but a brand new challenge dawns - or is it?

Analysis from Sky Sports' Callum Bishop:

"One point from three games. Zero goals and just one shot on target. Key names like Morgan Rogers, Youri Tielemans and Ollie Watkins gone. Some might say this is a new mountain for Unai Emery to climb as Aston Villa boss. And what a mountain.

"Let's not forget last season though. It took Villa five games to get off the mark in terms of goals in the league. They didn't win a game until the end of September. By Christmas, there were suggestions they were even in a title fight.

"That's how quickly fortunes and perceptions can change in the Premier League, and Emery has shown he knows just how to overcome this very obstacle. If he couldn't he wouldn't have been celebrating his 200th game in charge of Aston Villa tonight.

"Is that to say that a similar turnaround is coming. No. He did still have Premier League proven talent to help him turn things around in attack. The signing of Ibrahim Mbaye is exciting. George Hemmings has potential. Nicolas Jackson brings energy. But you'd probably back none of them to be more clinical than Watkins inside the 18-yard-box.

"But Emery has time and again found a way. He even said post-match that this is the position he found himself in last season. He's reminded his players of that. So, while the table looks bleak and the lack of goals is a talking point, refrain from jumping to conclusions. Villa's boss is playing the cards he's been dealt and as Jamie Carragher and Thierry Henry have already argued, there's few better at doing so."

What the result means and next fixtures...

images.caption: Image: Unai Emery reached 200 games in charge of Aston Villa

articles.title: La roja a De Frutos, un grave problema para el Rayo
articles.standfirst: Camello y Beñat San José manifestaron tras el partido que las tres rojas fueron excesivas
articles.summary: Camello y Beñat San José manifestaron tras el partido que las tres rojas fueron excesivas
articles.body: El Rayo consiguió la primera victoria de la temporada en LaLiga tras remontar al Racing en un partido luchado. Sin embargo, esos tres puntos pasarán factura, ya que el conjunto vallecano vio hasta tres tarjetas rojas. La más significativa la que le mostró Quintero González a Jorge De Frutos en el minuto 90. El extremo llevaba ya fuera del campo más de 20 minutos. Sin embargo, todo lo desencadenó la roja a Fran Pérez sobre el verde, tras un codazo. El banquillo del equipo madrileño protestó la expulsión. Fruto de esa reacción, vio la roja el encargado del balón parado del Rayo, Iban Fagoaga Aguirre. Y unos pocos minutos después, De Frutos protestó una decisión arbitral dándole supuestamente una patada a una nevera. Tras ello, el colegiado decidió expulsarle. Tres bajas muy significativas para su siguiente escenario, el Santiago Bernabéu. Sergio Camello habló de ello tras el partido. "La imagen que vemos de Fran para mi es exagerada para una roja. Por suerte no nos podemos quejar porque hemos conseguido los tres puntos. Lo de De Frutos, ahora hay muchas cámaras y se podrá ver si ha sido él y si no corregirlo. También te digo, una patada a una nevera no es una agresión a una persona y no creo que sea motivo para sacar una roja. Han sacado tres rojas dudosas", afirmó el delantero. Beñat San José también se pronunció sobre las tres expulsiones a su equipo. "Nos han expulsado a tres. Todos los banquillos tenemos sangre caliente y nos alteramos. No es algo sencillo, mi asistente que se encarga del balón parado y Jorge De Frutos por una patada a una nevera. Y la de Fran va abajo. Mi opinión es que no eran rojas", señaló el técnico rayista. Sin embargo, no es ese el motivo que puso Quintero González en el acta en la expulsión de Jorge De Frutos. "Por salir del banquillo gritando y gesticulando de forma reiterada, protestando una de mis decisiones de manera ostensible", es el motivo que señaló el colegiado de la tarjeta roja al futbolista del Rayo. Tres puntos vitales, pero que traen duras consecuencias.

images.caption: Jorge De Frutos Jorge De Frutos vía Instagram

articles.title: Beñat San José: "Camello tiene que seguir trabajando porque sabe que le voy a exigir todavía más"
articles.standfirst: El técnico franjirrojo realizó unas valoraciones del encuentro ante el Racing
articles.summary: El técnico franjirrojo realizó unas valoraciones del encuentro ante el Racing
articles.body: El Rayo Vallecano de Beñat San José consiguió su primera victoria de la temporada. Fue ante el Racing de Santander en un duelo emocionante y en el que el cuadro franjirrojo se puso el mono de trabajo, tras ponerse por detrás en dos ocasiones. Los grandes protagonistas del encuentro fueron Andrei Ratiu, que anotó el primer gol en su vuelta a la titularidad, tras su suplencia ante el Barcelona y el otro fue Sergio Camello que volvió a marcar un doblete y ya es el máximo goleador de LaLiga empatado a cinco tantos con Raphinha. El técnico vasco repasó los aspectos más significativos del duelo como las expulsiones, la vuelta a Vallecas o el espectacular momento de forma de su delantero. Victoria: "Muy importante, nos hacía falta. No solo era el ganar sino el cómo. Hemos hecho un partido espectacular, muy completo. Los jugadores han estado perfectos y han ejecutado el plan de partido tal y como hemos practicado entre semana. Las expulsiones nos han dolido mucho. Nos hemos quedado con tres expulsados en un abrir y cerrar de ojos. Le queremos dedicar esta victoria a Augusto Batalla". Camello: "Es muy completo, trabaja muchísimo para el equipo. Lleva el ADN de nuestro estilo de juego. Es un 9 que te puede meter un gol o asistir y también puede hacer de falso 9 o de 10 para generar superioridad entre líneas. Tiene que seguir trabajando porque sabe que le voy a exigir todavía más". Expulsiones: "Los árbitros me han dicho que la expulsión a Jorge De Frutos ha sido por darle una patada a una nevera. No he visto su informe. Respeto mucho a los árbitros y nos podemos equivocar todos, pero expulsar a un jugador así es fuerte. Lo de Fran es decisión de ellos, pero mi opinión es que ha sido un lance del juego, un movimiento natural que no es para que sea roja. No sé por qué han expulsado a mi asistente, no he sentido que hubiera ningún insulto desde el banquillo". Vuelta a Vallecas: "Es tan importante como jugar bien, como llevar nuestra camiseta, nuestro escudo, como entrenar... La afición en nuestro estadio es clave. Viniendo a Leganés he sentido como apoyan los aficionados, imagínate en Vallecas. Los aficionados tienen todo el derecho a manifestarse y a pedir jugar en nuestro campo porque es lo que queremos todos y les apoyamos. Si está todo en orden, tenemos que jugar en nuestro estadio".

images.caption: Beñat San José LALIGA

articles.title: Al Ittihad frena a Cristiano Ronaldo y su Al Nassr
articles.standfirst: Un doblete de Ilenikhena hace más líder a Al Hilal
articles.summary: Un doblete de Ilenikhena hace más líder a Al Hilal
articles.body: El Al Nassr de Cristiano Ronaldo, Joao Félix y Postecoglou rompió su arranque impoluto de temporada en Yeda. El vigente campeón de la liga saudí sucumbió (2-1) ante el Al Ittihad de Ilenikhena, que firmó doblete en cuestión de 20 minutos. Cristiano, que fue titular, se marchó sin marcar. Al Nassr lo había ganado todo y apuntaba, junto a Al Hilal, a ser el máximo favorito a ganar la liga saudí. Pero sufrió su primer revés en su visita al campo del Al Ittihad de Wissing. El nigeriano Ilenikhena, ex del Mónaco, encarriló el triunfo con dos tantos en 20 minutos. Aouar, ex de la Roma, asistió en el segundo. Fue un partido igualado y, en realidad, Al Nassr tuvo más ocasiones... pero Rakjovic, ex portero del Mallorca, sostuvo a Ittihad. Solamente Angelo, aún en la primera parte, pudo batirlo. El triunfo de Ittihad deja a Al Hilal como líder en solitario con 15 puntos en cinco jornadas. Al Nassr, segundo, se queda a tres; Al Ittihad está a cuatro de la cabeza.

images.caption: Ilenikhena celebra uno de sus goles. AL ITTIHAD.

articles.title: Ohio State's Chris Henry Jr., son of former NFL WR, catches a TD on his first career collegiate reception
articles.summary: Henry Jr. was a five-star recruit in the class of 2026 and had been committed to Ohio State since the summer of 2023.
articles.body:
Chris Henry Jr.'s first Ohio State catch went for a touchdown.

The freshman wide receiver caught a 15-yard TD from Tavien St. Clair late in the fourth quarter of the Buckeyes' 56-3 win over Ball State. Henry, a five-star recruit, was one of the best players in the high school class of 2026.

The son of former NFL and West Virginia wide receiver Chris Henry originally committed to the Buckeyes in the summer of 2023. He was the top wide receiver in the country and the No. 11 player in the 2026 recruiting class. The only other player from California who was ranked ahead of Henry on signing day was Texas A&M cornerback Brandon Arrington.

Though he didn't get much playing time in the Buckeyes' season-opener Saturday, Henry is poised to be one of Ohio State's next star wide receivers. Jeremiah Smith, Ohio State's current star wide receiver and a favorite for the 2026 Heisman, had eight catches for 151 yards and two scores in the first half before getting to watch the second half from the sidelines.

Smith struck Desmond Howard's Heisman pose after each of his touchdowns after Miami's Malachi Toney did the same thing following all three of his touchdowns in the Hurricanes' thrashing of Stanford on Friday night.

Overall, 14 different Ohio State players caught a pass against Ball State. Only five players had multiple receptions as backups got plenty of work.

Henry's father had nearly 1,900 yards over two seasons at West Virginia before he was a third-round pick of the Cincinnati Bengals in 2005. Chris Henry Sr. had a tumultuous NFL career that was plagued by multiple arrests and an eight-game suspension in 2007. In December of 2009, when Chris Henry Jr. was 2, the elder Henry died after he fell out of the back of a moving truck in the midst of a dispute with his fiancée. Chris Henry Jr. was one of three children the couple had together.

After Chris Henry Sr.'s death, his former West Virginia and Bengals teammate Adam "Pacman" Jones helped raise the children and Chris Henry Jr. lived with Jones and his family before he transferred to Mater Dei High School in California.

articles.title: El Ajax cae ante el PSV en una mala noche de Ter Stegen
articles.standfirst: El ex portero del Barcelona falló en el primer gol
articles.summary: El ex portero del Barcelona falló en el primer gol
articles.body: Fue una mala noche para el Ajax en el 'Topper' de la Eredivisie. Los de Míchel perdieron en Ámsterdam 1-3 ante un buen PSV que se pone como líder. Ter Stegen, que falló en el primer tanto de los de Eindhoven, no estuvo bien. El Ajax se queda, por ahora, a seis puntos del liderato. A los cuatro minutos ya ganaba el PSV. Ricardo Pepi anotó de cabeza tras un centro que no midió bien Ter Stegen. El vigente campeón de la Eredivisie arrancó mucho mejor el partido y aunque Arokodare pudo igualar el duelo... el gol de Geertruida justo antes del descanso volvió a ser un palo tremendo para el Ajax. Ya en la recta final, mientras el Ajax se volcaba para empatar, Bajraktarevic sentenciaba el partido con el 1-3 final. Los de Ámsterdam, con un partido pendiente en Eredivisie, suman su primera derrota del curso... pero ya empataron en casa (2-2) ante el Heerenveen. Se pueden quedar a ocho puntos de un AZ Alkmaar que tiene un partido pendiente aún.

articles.title: Football gossip: Sarr, Schade, Richarlison, Arteta, Hall, Onana, Benzema
articles.summary: Liverpool may make another move for Crystal Palace winger Ismaila Sarr in January and Tottenham's Richarlison may look for a Saudi switch.
articles.body:
Liverpool may make another move for Crystal Palace winger Ismaila Sarr in January, Tottenham 's Richarlison may look to Saudi switch as Trabzonspor transfer fails to materialise and Manchester United continuing to monitor Newcastle United 's Lewis Hall.

Liverpool will consider making another move to sign Ismaila Sarr from Crystal Palace in January after failing to agree a deal for the 28-year-old Senegal winger before the summer deadline. (Football Insider) , external

Tottenham 's wantaway Brazil forward Richarlison will be hoping to seal a move to the Saudi Pro League, where signings are permitted up to 12 October, after failing to secure a switch to Trabzonspor before the transfer window closed in Turkey on Friday. (Standard) , external

Arsenal are closing in on agreeing a new contract with manager Mikel Arteta, whose current deal runs out at the end of this season as they also make progress on new deals for 27-year-old England midfielder Declan Rice, Norway playmaker Martin Odegaard, 27, and Dutch defender Jurrien Timber, 25. (Teamtalk) , external

Arsenal enquired about Germany winger Kevin Schade in the summer but moved on as Brentford had no intention of selling the 24-year-old. (Teamtalk) , external

Manchester United will continue to monitor Newcastle United left-back Lewis Hall, 21, with a view to a possible move for the England international next summer. (Football Insider) , external

Belgium midfielder Amadou Onana has signed a new deal, which runs until 2031, with Aston Villa . (Sacha Tavolieri) , external

AC Milan are still interested in Sporting defender Goncalo Inacio, 25, and could make a move for the Portugal international in the January transfer window. (Tuttomercatoweb - in Italian) , external

Manchester United remain in talks about signing English midfielder Louis Page from Leicester City after they failed to complete a move for the 18-year-old on transfer deadline day. (Manchester Evening News via Evening Standard) , external

Lyon considered bringing former France striker Karim Benzema back to the club but the 38-year-old's contract as an ambassador with the Saudi Pro League prevented him from making the move. (L'Equipe - in French) , external

articles.title: Mario Hermoso y Soulé lideran una remontada épica y hacen soñar a Roma
articles.standfirst: 'La Loba' levanta en el descuento el partido ante Atalanta en otro recital de fútbol
articles.summary: 'La Loba' levanta en el descuento el partido ante Atalanta en otro recital de fútbol
articles.body: No podía perder la Roma. Los de Gasperini (que suman tres victorias en tres partidos) volvieron a protagonizar un fútbol excelso (el mejor de Italia, junto al Como) y remontaron en el descuento ante Atalanta. Mario Hermoso y Matías Soulé pusieron la guinda a un partido brillante de 'La Loba': 39 disparos, dos remates al palo y apenas seis 'chuts' concedidos al rival. El primer tiempo claramente de la Roma. El equipo de Gasperini llegaba 'volando' (4-0 a la Fiorentina y 0-4 al Lecce) y parecía que podía arrasar también a Atalanta. Pero se topó con Carnesecchi y chocó contra su propia falta de acierto. 18 disparos en 45 minutos... y cero tantos. Malen, que venía de hacer cinco tantos en dos partidos, no despegaba. Y eso Atalanta lo castigó. A los pocos momentos de arrancar la segunda parte, y tras una gran jugada de Charles De Ketelaere, Ederson golpeaba al Olímpico haciendo el 0-1. Encajaba 'La Loba' su primer gol del curso. Parecía que no iba a ser la noche de la Roma. Más de 30 disparos y el empate no llegaba. Carnesecchi, que acumuló nueve paradas y estaba inmenso, frenaba todo. Ni los palos ayudaron y Santiago Castro, que entró en el segundo tiempo, se topó con la madera en dos ocasiones. Y entonces llegó la mayor de las locuras. Mario Hermoso, que ha arrancado la temporada a un nivel altísimo, empató de cabeza tras saque de esquina botado por Soulé. Un gran remate que sorprendió a la Atalanta. Instantes después, ya en el descuento, el propio Soulé hizo el 2-1. Merecidísimo. Esta Roma tiene madera de competir el 'Scudetto'.

images.caption: Mario Hermoso celebra el 1-1 de la Roma. EFE.

articles.title: Boise State takes lead over No. 2 Oregon a play after officials miss an obvious penalty on an Oregon muffed punt
articles.summary: Jameson Perry almost ran into Evan Stewart before Stewart muffed a punt. But no flag was thrown.
articles.body:
Did Boise State get a touchdown because of an egregiously missed call by the officials in its game at Oregon on Saturday?

Broncos running back Sire Gaines scored on a 38-yard catch-and-run to give Boise State a 14-7 lead in the second quarter a play after Oregon's Evan Stewart muffed a punt after calling for a fair catch.

However, Boise State should have been penalized on the punt. Take a look:

Stewart should have been given a clean opportunity to make that catch. While Boise State's Jameson Perry didn't make contact with Stewart, he was exceptionally close to the wide receiver as he tracked the ball. And that itself is a foul.

According to the NCAA's rule book, if a player "is located where they could catch a free kick or a scrimmage kick that has crossed the neutral zone, and if the player is attempting to do so, they must be given an unimpeded opportunity to catch the kick." Further, "it is an interference foul if, before the receiver touches the ball, [an opposing player] enters the area defined by the width of the receiver's shoulders and extending one yard in front of him. When in question it is a foul."

Perry was clearly within three feet of Stewart's face. However, the penalty wasn't called on the field and is also not reviewable. Since it is a judgment call, kick-catch interference isn't subject to replay review or a challenge.

articles.title: La Liga tiene una nueva estrella
articles.standfirst: Aubameyang culmina la remontada ante el Villarreal con un gol en el minuto 88
articles.summary: Aubameyang culmina la remontada ante el Villarreal con un gol en el minuto 88
articles.body: Es el nombre propio de este inicio de temporada en LaLiga EA Sports. Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang volvió a marcar, como en cada una de las cuatro jornadas que van disputadas. Y esta vez fue al final, para confirmar la remontada gallega en La Cerámica. Para firmar una exhibición que vino acompañada de dos asistencias en los goles anteriores. El Deportivo tiene nuevo ídolo. Esta es la liga de Aubameyang Con permiso de Raphinha y Mbappé, el gran protagonista de este arranque es un delantero africano de 37 años que aterrizó en La Coruña dispuesto a hacerse un hueco en el corazón del aficionado gallego. Va camino de ello y quizá también de convertirse en el ídolo que necesitaba un club que vuelve a soñar en grande. Apenas van cuatro jornadas pero el Dépor vuelve a ser EuroDépor. Efímero, pasajero, seguramente, pero con la dosis suficiente de ilusión para recuperar la sonrisa. Los despachos de Riazor pueden colgarse la medalla. Traer al gabonés va camino de convertirse en la operación más acertada de toda esta Liga. Cuatro jornadas, cuatro goles y ante el Villarreal, además, dos asistencias. Todo ello traducido en ocho puntazos para meter a los de Antonio Hidalgo en puestos de Liga de Campeones. Para frotarse los ojos. El plan de juego en este equipo es claro. Sabe sufrir, se adapta a los diferentes escenarios que le propone el partido y responde en todos y cada uno de ellos. No es fácil levantarse de dos golpes consecutivos en La Cerámica. El Villarreal, que está en fase de encontrarse con su nuevo proyecto, tuvo el partido en su mano pero se le acabó escapando en cada una de las apariciones de Aubameyang. Salió dominador el equipo de Iñigo, que puso en liza a Logan Costa en el centro de la zaga y a Saliba en la medular junto a Gueye. Siempre bajo la batuta de Gerard Moreno, el equipo amarillo comenzó a sumar llegadas. En una de ellas, Pépé abrió el marcador y puso al Dépor contra las cuerdas. Fue el momento más delicado para los gallegos, que resistieron en una fase donde seguramente el partido se les pudo escapar de manera definitiva. Esa resiliencia de los gallegos encontró su punto álgido al filo del descanso. Antes, Aubameyang ya había avisado en un par de buenas ocasiones. En la tercera, penetró por el carril zurdo, la puso son suavidad al punto de penalti y Luismi Cruz agradeció el servicio con un preciso golpeo cruzado. Siempre dio la sensación que el Villarreal iba un paso por delante en el partido. O eso quiso el Deportivo que su rival creyese. Moleiro se encontró con Leo Román en un mano a mano y los de Iñigo cercaron la portería gallega en busca del segundo. Gueye lo rozó en un gol bien anulado. Mientras, se movieron los banquillos y ahí se agitó todo. En una acción muy desafortunada, Adama Traoré firmó un debut para el olvido con un golazo de cabeza en propia puerta. Un despeje desproporcionado en potencia, acompañado de colocación, que se convirtió en la solución de un Villarreal atascado. Sin tiempo para asimilarlo, Antonio Hidalgo rectificó un cambio ya pactado y dio entrada a Zakaria. Mano de santo para los gallegos. El gallego, en su primera acción, definió tras otra asistencia de Aubameyang. El gabonés remató la faena en el 88'. En una acción marca de la casa. Al espacio, con su velocidad punta inalterable a sus 37 castañas. Esa galopada la acompañó de una definició letal, como acostumbra. Y ahí se acabó todo. Demostración más que suficiente de que estamos ante uno de los grandes delanteros de esta Liga. Argumento sólido para creer en un Deportivo capaz de grandes cosas esta temporada. El tiempo, ese del que se burla Aubameyang, confirmará o desmentirá ese nuevo propósito gallego.

articles.title: El Mallorca no puede con un rocoso y muy serio Eldense
articles.standfirst: Álex Sala estrelló un penalti en el poste y los baleares siguen sin ganar fuera en un partido vistoso de ambos, pero cándido en las áreas
articles.summary: Álex Sala estrelló un penalti en el poste y los baleares siguen sin ganar fuera
articles.body: El Mallorca no pudo ganar en el Pepico Amat al no pasar del empate sin goles ante un Eldense que suma así su segundo punto, ambos en casa, y deja por primera vez su portería a cero. Los bermellones, que fallaron un penalti antes del descanso, siguen sin ganar lejos de Son Moix después de dos desplazamientos. El Eldense apostaba por seguir su dinámica de sensaciones y meter mano un Mallorca que quería seguir en el tren de cabeza. Intercambio de balón y posesión en un arranque de más posesión que profundidad, hasta que Álex Sala camino de la media hora puso a prueba a Ramón Vila. La estrategia a balón parado cerca estuvo de premiar al Mallorca tras un zarpazo de Darder que Vila evitaba en una serie de saques de esquina consecutivos, mientras Luvumbo tampoco acertaba, mientras la respuesta azulgrana la mandó a las nubes Fidel desde cerca. Sobre la bocina Morlanes aprovechó una pérdida local para que recortar a la zaga local, derribándole Jesús Clemente. Pero la ejecución del penalti en cuestión la estrelló con potencia Álex Sala en el poste, concediendo al descanso una vida extra al Eldense. La segunda parte comenzó con otro 'picotazo' visitante pero el remate de Adri Fuentes lo despejó, no sin apuros, un acertado Ramón Vila, pero poco a poco el Eldense fue nivelando el partido, se cerró mucho mejor y no sufrió tanto como en el primer tiempo, ante un Mallorca que intentó sacar tajada en banda izquierda con asiduidad. Había batalla y brega como intenciones de ir arriba a la vez del temor de ser cazado a la contra, algo que al Eldense le hizo por momentos tener mayor dificultad ofensiva. Así, en la recta final David Ruiz, para los locales, y Pablo Torre, de falta directa para los baleares, lo intentaron pero sin éxito y el partido concluyó como empezó: con las 'gafas' en el marcador, con lo que resultaba de justicia el reparto de puntos.

articles.title: Espiau salva in extremis a un pobre Zaragoza
articles.standfirst: Un gol del delantero evitó el primer traspiés en casa ante el Antequera
articles.summary: Un gol del delantero evitó el primer traspiés en casa ante el Antequera
articles.body: El Real Zaragoza sigue abonado al sufrimiento pero esta vez la moneda cayó de cara cuando nadie lo esperaba ya. Un gol de Espiau en el descuento evitó el segundo tropiezo de los de Ibai Gómez y sirvió para derrotar a un valiente Antequera. Ander falló un penalti y el ariete alivió la angustia de toda la gente dando el primer triunfo. Se esperaba que los aragoneses dieran continuidad al juego que mostraron en Tarragona pero el que salió dominando y perdonando goles fue el cuadro de Abraham Paz. Moi Parra y Destiny eran un dolor de muelas para la defensa y Westerveld y Diego González, sobre la línea, salvaron dos goles visitantes. Los maños reaccionaron tímidamente con una buena jugada que mando Pau Sans el balón a las nubes. Fue un espejismo, ya que el Antequera fue el dueño y señor de la primera parte y tan solo le faltó el gol. La afición zaragocista, pese a todo, mantuvo su apoyo. Imposible pedirle más. En el descanso, Ibai Gómez introdujo tres cambios para cambiar el guión y el Real Zaragoza mejoró levemente. Tomó el control del partido pero sin peligro hasta que Sangalli fue derribado en el área a falta de 20 minutos. Penalti. Ander Herrera quiso ser el héroe y acabó siendo el villano tras fallar la pena máxima. Entre el palo y el portero evitaron el tanto. Fue el primer disparo a puerta del conjunto blanquillo. En el tramo final, Espiau falló un gol sin portero tras un grave error de Alcover, que luego se repuso con una gran parada. Cuando todos daban por hecho el empate, Diego González salvó un balón que se iba fuera, logró centrar y Espiau de una forma poco ortodoxa empujó el balón a la red. Un triunfo balsámico en un flojo partido de los locales. Mucho por mejorar pero con tres puntos es más fácil. FICHA TÉCNICA: 1-Real Zaragoza: Westerveld, Gabilondo (Sangalli 46'), Diego González, Iranzo, Escudero (Pereira 46'), Ander Herrera, Terrer, Cuenca (Jardí 46), Vadillo (Ureña 72'), Pau Sans (Espiau 80') y Delgado. Entrenador: Ibai Gómez 0-Antequera: Alcover, Antón, Quintana, Iván Pérez, Julio Martínez, Gené (Agüero 60'), Bassele, Aspra (Mangada 46'), Moi Parra (Isra 60'), Luismi (Almagro 81') y Destiny (Zarzana 60') Entrenador: Abraham Paz Goles: 1-0 Espiau 90'. Árbitro: Joan Masip Vidal (Colegio catalán). Amonestó a Aspra 22', Moi Parra 44', Iranzo 49' e Iván Pérez 62. Estadio: Ibercaja Estadio con 13.248 espectadores.

articles.title: Hidalgo: “Es una victoria brutal ante un equipo Champions”
articles.standfirst: El técnico del Dépor alabó el esfuerzo de su equipo y asegura que el objetivo sigue siendo la salvación
articles.summary: El técnico del Dépor alabó el esfuerzo de su equipo y asegura que el objetivo sigue siendo la salvación
articles.body: El entrenador del Deportivo aseguró después del partido que el trabajo del equipo fue muy bueno y que es una victoria de prestigio ante un equipo de Champions. “Esto es muy largo, queda menos para la salvación, aún faltan muchos puntos para el objetivo del club que es la permanencia. Hemos conseguido una victoria brutal ante un gran equipo”. Para Hidalgo es un gran paso por los jugadores que están debutando en la categoría y que se han levantado después de los goles en contra. “Al final los rivales de Primera te exigen mucho, hay que ser valientes y tenemos valentía y pegada y eso es una gran virtud”. “Tenéis que ver cómo entrena y la sonrisa que contagia a todos”, así está de encantado el míster del Deportivo con su estrella. Para el catalán la ilusión que tiene el vestuario es un motor fantástico. “Tengo suerte de tener jugadores con hambre y de mucha calidad, hay que seguir trabajando duro y pelear ante el Getafe otros tres puntos”, expresó.

articles.title: One former Cal Bear named a Week 1 captain for UCLA football
articles.summary: Jaivian Thomas and Cole Martin were named Week 1 captains for the UCLA Bruins, joining Nico Iamaleava and Sammy Omosigho.
articles.body:
Earlier this week the UCLA Bruins announced that quarterback Nico Iamaleava and linebacker Sammy Omosigho were named the team's permanent captains for the 2026 season.

On Saturday, UCLA announced that running back Jaivian Thomas and safety Cole Martin being named gameday captains for the Bruins ' Week 1 showdown versus the Cal Bears.

The game will be extra special for Thomas, as he spent his first two NCAA seasons with Cal before heading south to join UCLA ahead of the 2025 season. Thomas' numbers took a step back in his first year with the Bruins, rushing for just 294 yards in 2025 after being at 626 with Cal in 2024.

The running back usage will be something to watch for Bob Chesney and Dean Kennedy's offense, with Wayne Knight and Anthony Woods joining Thomas in the backfield.

Martin didn't play for the Golden Bears but the safety has played for Oregon, Arizona State and now the Bruins, meaning he has plenty of West Coast college football under his belt preparing him for Saturday night's showdown.

Martin made 65 tackles for UCLA in 2025, with one interception and three passes defensed. Martin was one of three Bruins to represent the school at this year's Big Ten Conference Media Day, joining fellow captains Iamaleava and Omosigho.

Kickoff is set for Saturday night at 7:30p.m. on ESPN, with UCLA heading to California Memorial Stadium as road favorites.

articles.body:
One member of the squad called upon by La Liga giants Barcelona for their upcoming meeting with Valencia will be omitted from the club's official matchday list. This comes owing to an overbooking in Hansi Flick's setup.

Barca are of course primed to return to action on Sunday, making the trip to Mestalla with sights on a fourth successive victory to open the defence of their La Liga title.

As is customary, the Catalans, in turn, unveiled their travelling party for the fixture online on Saturday afternoon:

As alluded to above, though, for one member of this squad, disappointment awaits… Hansi Flick's call-up to face Valencia features 24 players, owing to the presence of the returning Gavi, and summer signing Gabriel Jesus.

And according to a report from journalist Sergi Capdevila, as a result:

'Flick faces his 1st painful decision of the season. With Gavi and Gabriel Jesus okay, he has 24 players available and only 23 can enter the squad list. First discard of the season incoming due to 'overbooking'.'

articles.title: No. 5 Texas vs. Texas State live updates: Horns lead 49-7 after three quarters
articles.summary: Stay updated on everything happening between the Longhorns and Bobcats.
articles.body:
AUSTIN, Texas — A season with high expectations gets under way for the No. 5 Texas Longhorns on Saturday against the Texas State Bobcats at Darrell K Royal-Texas Memorial Stadium in a prelude to the No. 1 Ohio State Buckeyes coming to the Forty Acres next week.

After Texas State received the opening kickoff, a touchback deep into the end zone, Texas gave up a first down on three short completions, but inflicted a tackle for loss on a second-down running play and got pressure on Bobcats quarterback Brad Jackson to force a throwaway on third down under pressure from fifth-year defensive tackle Hero Kanu.

A bad snap to the Texas State punter impacted his rhythm, leading to a shank out of bounds only 17 yards past the line of scrimmage, affording Texas favorable field position at its own 44-yard line.

Lined up in 12 personnel, the first touch went to senior running back Hollywood Smothers, who bounced the run outside behind blocks from sophomore tight end Nick Townsend and junior wide receiver Ryan Wingo, made two defenders miss in the open field, and got down the sideline for a 45-yard gain.

Two plays later, on 3rd and 5, junior wide receiver Cam Coleman beat an attempt to jam him at the line of scrimmage and left the Texas State cornerback falling to the ground on an easy six-yard touchdown catch, his first touch for the Longhorns.

With the Bobcats facing 3rd and 11, the Longhorns made their first big mistake of the season when sophomore cornerback Kade Phillips was flagged for pass interference down the sideline on a hopeful throw by Jackson. Texas State was able to gain another first down, but when Jackson pulled the ball, senior linebacker Rasheem Biles had contain. Going for it on fourth down, Jackson had his pass batted down at the line of scrimmage by junior defensive tackle Alex January for a turnover on downs.

Facing its own fourth down, senior quarterback Arch Manning found Wingo on a wheel route before connecting with senior tight end Spencer Shannon for 11 yards, the first career target and catch for the Mater Dei product. On the next play, Wingo found the end zone on jet sweep, a pass credited to Manning that turned into an eight-yard touchdown with help from Shannon and Townsend blocking on the edge.

On a drive that started with a 22-yard run by Jaylen Jenkins, Texas State created another explosive play when Jackson scrambled to find an outlet receiver down the sideline for 25 yards to the Texas 5-yard line. A one-yard gain up the middle ended the first quarter.

The Texas defense forced Jackson to hold the ball long enough for Phillips to break up a pass in the end zone and force 3rd and goal from the 4-yard line after GJ Kinne used his first timeout of the first half. The play call by Kinne wasn't an effective one, as Kanu created quick penetration to create a tackle for loss, forcing a field-goal attempt that missed wide left from 24 yards.

Able to stand in the pocket on second down, Wingo worked open for a 16-yard reception before Smothers found a seam outside for nine yards. Running downhill on his first college carry, freshman Derrek Cooper moved the chains, but freshman wide receiver Jermaine Bishop quickly put the Horns off schedule by dropping a screen pass.

Cooper ended up leaving the field during the first half with an apparent injury.

It didn't hurt Texas as head coach Steve Sarkisian dialed up a screen pass to Smothers that featured Townsend as an escort for the first down. After a check down to Smothers and a run by fifth-year running back Raleek Brown produced 3rd and 1, Sarkisian used his first timeout of the half, sparking frustration with the officials.

With sophomore running back Michael Terry III in the game in a two-back set, Smothers took a carry up the middle for the first down and Townsend caught a short pass for nine yards. Needing to convert another 3rd and 1, a pin and pull for Brown included a nice cut by the USC and Arizona State transfer for a 13-yard touchdown and a 21-0 margin with 7:53 remaining in the second quarter.

The first forced turnover of the season for Texas came from Biles, who knocked the ball loose on a running play. Sophomore nickel back Graceson Littleton scooped it up with some momentum and out-raced Texas State to the end zone for a 59-yard touchdown return.

Down 28-0, Texas State fought back, taking advantage of a busted coverage by Texas for a 41-yard completion and lost contain on Jackson in the pocket on a 33-yard scramble. A four-yard touchdown run finished the drive as the Longhorns defense found itself off balance.

With 3:59 remaining in the second quarter, the Horns had a chance to respond, but it started poorly, as senior kickoff returner Ryan Niblett fumbled the ball in the end zone, forcing the drive to start at the 10-yard line after his recovery.

A nine-yard completion to Wingo and a two-yard run by Smothers moved the chains as Texas operated without much urgency. A 30-yard gain by Wingo as Manning scrambled was reduced to 19 yards on a holding penalty on junior wide receiver Emmett Mosley V heading into the two-minute warning. It could have been an even bigger play — Coleman was running free in the Texas State secondary, but Manning didn't see him.

Out of the timeout, Manning made an even worse decision, holding the ball after getting flushed from the pocket and taking an unnecessary sack. A completion to Mosley into a tight window helped make it for it, but left the Longhorns still looking for a big play to flip the field before halftime.

Manning found it quickly despite facing 3rd and 15, dropping a pass into Wingo's hands down the sidelines after a double move that gained 45 yards.

A throw to Mosley over the middle picked up another first down, but Texas was running out of time after opting to run a running play after the completion instead of calling a timeout. Sarkisian was forced to use his second anyway, with only 16 seconds left on the clock and the ball at the 11-yard line.

The Longhorns had a chance to score before halftime, but Wingo couldn't come up with a difficult catch in the end zone and Manning committed a cardinal sin, throwing late and over the middle for an interception that effectively ended the first half.

Manning had a chance for a big play early when Sarkisian called a go route for Coleman on a 3rd and 2. The Auburn transfer won his route and Manning connected with him, but the ball was slightly underthrown, limiting the gain to 44 yards.

After Texas State helped Texas with an offside penalty on 3rd and 7, Manning and Coleman connected again over the middle as Coleman showed off his strong hands to finish the 20-yard touchdown catch for a 35-7 lead.

The Longhorns defense flashed its opportunism again when junior defensive tackle Maraad Watson forced a fumble and junior edge Colin Simmons recovered.

Texs converted the sudden-change possession as Manning scrambled for 11 yards on 3rd and 15 to set up a nice touch pass to Mosley breaking to the sideline. After sophomore tight end Emaree Winston rumbled for 18 yards, Smothers bailed out a possession that was on the verge of stalling by catching a short pass, making a defender miss, and diving for the end zone on 3rd and 12 from the 13-yard line for a 42-7 lead.

The Longhorns defense imposed itself on the ensuing possession. First, converted cornerback Kobe Black delivered a crunching hit on Texas State wide receiver Chris Dawn Jr. to force an incompletion, then Biles read a screen pass and jumped it to come up with the first interception of the season for Texas.

That ended the day for Manning and the Longhorns starters as sophomore quarterback KJ Lacey came in the game and immediately delivered a dart to Bishop on a rollout with a defender in his face.

Brown finished the drive by hitting a seam and scoring from 21 yards out, one of the easier touchdowns he'll score this season to put Texas up 49-7.

articles.title: Arch Manning and new weapon Cam Coleman show instant connection vs. Texas State
articles.summary: Manning and Coleman connected for two TDs in Texas' season opener.
articles.body:
Texas began its 2026 campaign on Saturday with a home game against Texas State, where the Longhorns debuted their new-look offense.

The Longhorns' offense from a year ago was led by running back Quintrevion Wisner and wide receivers Ryan Wingo, DeAndre Moore Jr., and Parker Livingstone. Only Wingo is with Texas at the start of this season.

Texas wasn't worried as it brought in a key transfer of its own in wide receiver Cam Coleman Jr.

He spent the first two seasons of his collegiate career at Auburn and combined for 1,306 yards and 12 touchdowns in 23 games.

Coleman wasted little time in endearing himself to his new fan base. Manning hit Coleman for a six-yard score in the first quarter, Texas' first touchdown of the season.

Later in the third quarter, the duo connected again. This time, Coleman came down with the 20-yard reception for another score.

The second touchdown showed Manning's ability to thread the needle and put the football through tight windows to his pass-catchers. The quarterback had attempted this type of pass into triple coverage in the end zone earlier in the game, but it was picked off. Manning's second attempt at it was successful to Coleman.

Coleman and Manning were pulled with 5:50 left in the third quarter, but that didn't stop either of them from showing off a connection that looks like it will be a problem for opposing defenses.

Coleman finished the day with 70 yards and two touchdowns on three receptions.

This was the third multi-score game of Coleman's career so far. He tallied three scores against Louisiana Monroe in 2024 when he was with Auburn, and had two in a 2024 win over Texas A&M that went into four overtimes.

Manning finished the day 20 of 27 passing for 305 yards, 4 touchdowns, and 1 interception. This was just the fourth time in his career with the Longhorns that the quarterback threw for four touchdowns in the same game.

Texas entered the season ranked No. 5 in the AP poll. While the Longhorns enjoyed a nice tune-up game on Saturday, they will have to refocus on business as before hosting No. 1 Ohio State next week.
